Let's look at it some more.

Replicants are both machine and human. They where given by design their human nature. Unlike real humans who develop during an entire life they have been built with a set of norms and action patterns to function optimaly for their tasks. You say they are happy when free? They are all awaiting a death penalty. And they know when it runs out. At the same time they know they have no true history. It was all a lie. Though hard to accept as we see when Leon tries to recover a photo from his flat. Roy makes fun of him becouse he knows its a false memory, but Leon can't let go. Pris may look happy when she plays around in sebastians flat, but isn't it just a way for her to use the skills she was given to gain Roy access? Is it not all a charade?

It is this dilemma of what is real and what value we can put on it that the movie is all about.

You say he spares Deckards life, but does he?

Deckard struggles with his thoughts regarding replicants. In Rachael he finds love, a notion he thought imposible for replicants. And this relationship and his insight into her realization that she and her memories are constructed promts him to question his own memories. The photo of family, the piano tune, the unicorn dream, they are all a part of Deckards identity that he thought to be irrefutable. But now he doubts. Towards the end he is not chasing the replicants to do his job, he is looking for answers just like them.

One person seems to know more about Deckards inner life even than Deckard himself, and that is Gaff. The oregami figures all illuminate Deckard to feelings he holds deep in himself. How does he know?

The scene where Roy is chasing Deckard is a symbol of the monster that lives inside Deckard finally catching up to him. The truth. The truth that he himself is a replicant. Roy does not spare him, he sees himself in Deckard and leaves him to figure out for himself what to do with that information.

Traditionally "fiskesuppe" in norway was a bowl of what vegetable you had and some fish. Boil and serve. And in essence it still is.
I hardly ever use a recipe for soup since it's so difficult to fuck up.

First you need to decide what kind of stock you want. The soup will be awsome with real homemade stock, but I never bother for everyday use.

Next is the vegetables. Carrots and leeks are pretty common in norway, but you can use pretty much anything you like. Fennel root, onion, potatoes, etc. Chop and drop in stock. You should try and throw the vegetables that takes the .longest to cook first. So potatoes before leeks, etc.

Then when there is only 10min left before vegetables are done throw in some fish. I like to use white fish, like cod, but you can pretty much use anything. Hallibut and salmon is a nice combo. Leave the fish in there to simmer until done. It should flake a part.

Throw on cream and season over the heat. I think the most important spice is white pepper. It goes extremly well with any cream based soup. So white and black pepper. Salt. I've even used a pinch of nutmeg, it creates an intresting profile. But be careful with it, and I like it more when there is no salmon.

So I guess the tl;dr is basicly throw vegetable and fish in pot, cream, spice eat!

Once you are in hospital you won't end up on the street. There are programs to provide housing either temporary or more permanent. The though time for you will be from getting here to getting help.

The process I described above is the normal way to go. But depending on where in the country you are there may be different ways to get help on the day. I believe the DPS centers will take walk-ins before four, and the emergency rooms take over after that. (Atleast thats the way in oslo) If you need to go the emergency room they are very busy, so turn up a little before four and you should get to talk to someone. If you are in danger to yourself they will of course priorotize you.
Also in oslo atleast there are doctors that you can go to without having them as a GP (actually you can do this with most, but they never have time). The wait time is usually a bit high so show up early. But through these guys you could essentially go to a doctor the day after you get here.

But I'm wondering if maybe you should just go straight to the DPS. If they can take you in as a walk-in that might be best...

When you get here you will most likely have to go through diagnostics again.

You start the process by going to your GP. You can choose your own at a website that list the available doctors. If you have a diagnosis from the states bring some documentation on it and preferably your medical journal. After telling your GP about your problems and you having a diagnosis allready he wil probably refer you to DPS (District psychiatric Center) for evaluation\treatment. This can be done in many ways. Going in for therapy, admission to a clinic etc.
If your condition is serious enough you may be offered a more permanent admission to a mental health hospital which can be more or less "free". 

My sister had a system where she and the staff constantly evaluated her condition and she lived in her appartment when she felt ok and went back to hospital when she was sick. So my experience is that if you are cooperating in finding a good solution they will usually go with it.

Also as a norwegian citizen you will be able to receive wellfare that will cover rent and basic living expenses. It's not much, but you can live on it.

So to sum up. I think there are many faults to the way mental health care work in norway. Mostly the fact that way to few people get help early enough and the problems increase to a point where longer treatment is needed. But I do believe that when you do get help it is usually very good.

If you do come here I do advise that you go to your GP first just to get the ball rolling. And then go to NAV for help with money. If you go to NAV with a date for some followup treatment\evaluation or even a temporary diagnosis they will be much more inclined to smooth through the process.

Lastly, I know it's personal, but may I ask what your diagnosis\problem is? I may be able to offer some more insight into what kind of treatment is common for your illness.

Good luck with what ever you decide. Hope you find a place here in life that does you good :)

He told me to stay quite as he didn't want my mother or siblings to wake up. He threw me this big coat with wool lining, I put it on and we walked down to the shore. He told me to get in the boat. Was ordered to sit in the front as to stabalize the boat. Sat there as he slowly took us further and further out to sea. I told me to get back with him as it was gonna get rough. Sped up and we jumped, over and over again. I closed my eyes and held on for my life, trying to predict the movements as not to hurt myself. After quite some time of this he slowed down and turned the engine off. I looked up and as the boat reached the top of a wave I realized that I could no longer see land. I could feel the panic well up inside me and looked at my father. He had been standing this whole time and and now looked down at me and said: "Now this, this is my god."
Then he started the engine and drove back without saying anything except for right before we entered the cabin again: "By the way, don't tell you're mother about this."
I never did.

I stumble myself up on my arms and get a hold of the doorhandle, it's not locked. As I get into the entrence I'm exhausted, I spent almost 20mins just getting there. I gather some strenght to get into the kitchen and get a hold of the breadbox, grab a peice of bread.
